newsitem.title: USA: US steps up anti-bribery effort, export promotion.
newsitem.headline: US steps up anti-bribery effort, export promotion.

text.p: U.S. trade officials said Tuesday they are stepping up efforts to encourage small businesses to export more and to discourage the use of bribery by foreign companies with U.S. subsidiaries.

Secretary of Commerce Mickey Kantor said at a news conference that bribery is one of the most difficult barriers to trade faced by U.S. businesses, who are forbidden by law to make illicit payments in order to win contracts abroad.
Kantor said the Commerce Department is changing its advocacy rules as they relate to U.S. subsidiaries of foreign companies to discourage bribery.

Kantor said that in order for U.S. affiliates of foreign companies to get Commerce Department advocacy support on contracts, the parents of those firms will have to have corporate anti-bribery policies in place.
They will also have to assure that no affiliates are paying bribes to win contracts for which U.S. assistance is requested, he said.
The Export-Import Bank is also taking steps to make sure that no bribery is taking place in projects that it supports, Kantor said.

"This was a way to address this issue quickly and hopefully effectively," Kantor said. "However, we believe it is going to take a whole panoply of approaches in order to finaly drive out bribery and corruption from the international trading system."

The anti-bribery initiative is one of a number of steps to lower trade barriers abroad and boost U.S. exports that were outlined by the Commerce Department in its "annual National Export Strategy Report" to Congress.

The report also outline a new effort to encourage smaller businesses to export. The Small Business Administration plans to extend its program that guarantees working capital for small business to support exports, the report said.

At the same time, The Ex-Im Bank is designing a pilot project to provide guarantess for bundled trade loans. The idea is to help jump-start a secondary market for trade loans to small businesses, it said.
